title: The North Face Dome 5 review: a five-person hub dome built for snow
dek: A four-season, five-person dome with a ring-shaped aluminum hub, three large doors and snow skirts. Here's what The North Face built into it, and what it weighs.
subject: The North Face Dome 5
verdict: The Dome 5 shrinks the big-dome idea to five people: a DAC frame with a ring-shaped aluminum hub, snow skirts, three big doors and a removable vestibule. At about 18 pounds it's a basecamp or sled-hauled tent. There are few owner reviews, so treat the claims below as the manufacturer's.
bestFor: Small expedition teams, snow camping with a sled or vehicle, basecamps in wind and snow.
notFor: Backpacking, summer car camping, or anyone wanting a quick, simple pitch.
pros: Ring-shaped aluminum hub reduces the number of poles
Three large double doors sized for expedition packs
Snow flaps, a snow skirt and a port window
About 136 sq ft of floor for five
cons: Published fabric specs disagree between listings
body:
## The short version

The Dome 5 is a five-person, four-season dome that The North Face describes as made for Alaskan backcountry adventure. It uses a DAC pole system joined by a ring-shaped aluminum hub, which cuts the number of separate poles while keeping the frame stable. There are few owner reviews online, so most of what follows is the manufacturer's description.

## Built for snow

External snow flaps and a snow skirt seal the base against blowing snow. Lift vents are meant to channel wind and reduce flapping, and a polyurethane port window, cold-tested to -60°F, lets you check the weather without opening a door.

## Doors and layout

Three large double doors are sized for expedition packs, and a removable vestibule can go on the sunny side. The canopy hangs inside the fly and is color-coded, and the fly attaches with a mix of sleeves and clips that The North Face calls Fusion pitch.

## Weight

Trail weight is about 18 pounds and total weight about 22. That's light for five people in a four-season shelter but heavy for any one person to carry, so plan on splitting it up or hauling it.

## A note on specs

Listings disagree on the fabrics: one gives a 70-denier canopy and 1,500 mm fly coating, the spec table a 40-denier canopy and 1,200 mm coating. If those numbers matter for your use, check the tag on the tent you're buying.

## Poles and parts

The Dome 5 uses **a hubbed pole set** (several legs joined at an aluminum hub), **DAC**.

As with the Dome 8, inspect the aluminum hub and every leg socket on a used Dome 5. A cracked hub is the one part that's hard to improvise around.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Dome 5 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Dome%205), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

The Dome 5 is a purpose-built snow and wind basecamp for small teams. If you need that, it's a capable design. If you don't, it's a lot of tent to haul.
